wars.outcome: Bern and Fribourg conquer Vaud in 1536 and Bern occupies the Genevan basin; by the Treaty of Lausanne of 1564 Savoy recovers the lands round Geneva and Bern keeps Vaud 'forever'.
wars.note: The Treaty of Lausanne (1564) page does not exist on Wikipedia (WebFetch url_not_found); the Republic of Geneva page is the source. The Chablais, Ternier and Gaillard cells are the researcher's reading.

wars.name: Valtellina War
belligerents: opponents not named by the pages
wars.outcome: The Three Leagues lost the Valtellina when rebels rose on 18/19 July 1620 (Graubünden page; History of Switzerland dates the loss to 1623, after the war from 1620); the Valtellina page gives a Valtellina War of 1620-1626 and a Treaty of Paris of February 1623. 'On 3 September 1639 the Leagues agreed with Spain to bring the Valtellina back under League sovereignty' (Graubünden page); the Cisalpine Republic annexed it on 10 October 1797.
wars.note: Repair 2026-10-25: the ledger now breaks the Leagues' tint 1620-1639; the Valtellina page ends the war in 1626 and the Graubünden page dates the return.

wars.name: French invasion of Switzerland

zones.text: all of Switzerland, 'completely overran' on 5 March 1798

wars.outcome: The Old Swiss Confederation collapsed; the Helvetic Republic, 'One and Indivisible', was proclaimed on 12 April 1798 without Geneva, Neuchatel and the Prince-Bishopric of Basel. Act of Mediation 19 February 1803.
wars.note: The Cisalpine Republic had annexed the Valtellina on 10 October 1797 (Three Leagues page).

wars.name: Sonderbund War
wars.outcome: The Diet dissolved the Sonderbund on 21 October 1847; 'The Sonderbund was easily defeated in less than a month; there were about 130 killed.' A federal constitution followed in 1848.
wars.note: A civil war within the Confederation; no border change.

wars.name: Neuchatel crisis
wars.outcome: Royalists 'launched an armed insurrection on 3 September 1856'; under the Treaty of Paris of 26 May 1857 the King of Prussia 'finally renounced his claims to Neuchatel'.
wars.note: Neuchatel was already a Swiss republic from 1 March 1848; the crisis changed no border.

certainty.note: Cantonal, bailiwick and associate frontiers were never surveyed; the Empire's legal frontier was loosened by the Peace of Basel (1499) and the Peace of Westphalia (1648) without a boundary line. 1799-1802 is the Helvetic Republic, drawn by the eu-20 dossier; 1803-1814 is the Mediation Confederation, drawn here from the shapes Cliopatria files under the Helvetic Republic.

The Congress of Vienna of 1814-15 recognised permanent Swiss neutrality and re-established Swiss independence, the Treaty of Turin (16 March 1816) extended Geneva's territory, and 'Switzerland's borders saw only minor adjustments thereafter'; the 1979 canton of Jura is internal.

notes:
Decision on the row: one dossier. Cliopatria's 'Swiss Confederation' (1294..2024, 59 shapes, with a gap 1799-1814 filled by its 'Helvetic Republic' row) is treated as ONE state, as the Switzerland page does ('Founded: 1 August 1291', 'Federal state: 12 September 1848'): the Old Confederacy to 1798, the Helvetic Republic (a different state, eu-20's dossier helvetic-republic), then the Confederation of the Mediation (1803), the Restoration (Federal Treaty of 7 August 1815) and the federal state (1848) are 'rename' events here, not new dossiers, so the colour stays. The break at 1798 is a loss of all land to helvetic-republic (5 March 1798) and a gain back from it on 19 February 1803 (the Act of Mediation, repair pass 2026-10-25), with the Valais, Neuchatel, the Jura and Geneva joining in 1815. If the colour agent prefers to split at 1798 or 1848, the keyframes and ledger divide cleanly at those years.

To fix in other dossiers: (1) Cliopatria's Helvetic Republic row runs 1799..1814 and so covers the Mediation Confederation of 1803-1813 (nineteen cantons) as well; this dossier now carries the 1803-1814 Mediation land (new keyframes 1803, 1806, 1811, 1814 and a gain from helvetic-republic on 19 February 1803), so helvetic-republic must end on 19 February 1803 and drop Cliopatria's shapes of 1803-1814. Its start should be 1798 (proclaimed 12 April 1798), or 1798 has no owner. (2) The Holy Roman Empire minor states dossier should carry the loss side of the gains here (Lucerne 1332, Zurich 1351, Glarus and Zug 1352, Bern 1353, Appenzell 1411, Schaffhausen 1454, Fribourg and Solothurn 1481, Basel 1501; Aargau 1415 and Thurgau 1460 are losses of house-of-habsburg) and the vassal relation 'Allegiance of Swiss Confederation to Holy Roman Empire' 1326-1458 (Cliopatria relation row); this dossier does not repeat it. Legal independence from the Empire is 1499 (de facto, Peace of Basel) and 1648 (Westphalia).

Associates (Zugewandte Orte). Cliopatria draws the Confederacy with its allies inside. Rule 4 says associations are never territory, so the keyframes remove Valais (Sieben Zenden, associate from 1416), Graubunden (the Three Leagues, allied 1497-98) with the Valtellina (the Leagues' subject land 1512-1797) and Geneva (ally from 1526, in the shape only 1540-1571), and the ledger tints them with vassal_start/vassal_end events whose counterpart is the associate (three-leagues, sieben-zenden, republic-of-geneva; none has a dossier, see counterparts_needing_dossiers). It is a status stretch: the associates were allies, not vassals, and the tint is the nearest rule-4 status. Associates not removed: the abbey and city of St. Gallen and Appenzell (drawn from 1459, absorbed as cantons; their gains are ledger events at confidence 2), Neuchatel (1-3 Cliopatria cells 1402-1847; a Prussian principality until 1848, a canton from 1814/1815), Mulhouse (associate from 1515 per the Old Swiss page; no Cliopatria cell) and the Prince-Bishopric of Basel (the Jura, 4 cells 1487-1797; the Helvetic Republic page calls it 'the old Prince-Bishopric of Basel' and excludes it from the Republic). No page opened dates the Neuchatel or Jura relations beyond the 1406 and 1526 treaties.

Corrections to Cliopatria: (a) the 1294 shape includes Zug and part of Lucerne and omits Obwalden; the Old Swiss Confederacy begins 1291 (new keyframe 1291). (b) Bern is drawn ten years late (1363 instead of 1353; new keyframe 1353). (c) Basel-Stadt is missing from every shape before 1815 although Basel joined in 1501. (d) Geneva is in no shape after 1571; the canton is added to every shape from 1815. (e) The Swiss shapes 1860-1950 flicker by single border cells (Ain, Doubs, Haute-Savoie, Haut-Rhin, Baden-Wurttemberg, South Tyrol): outline noise, not events. Area check: infobox 41,291 km2 (no year) against 40,201 km2 in 1815 (0.97) and 40,677 km2 in 1950 (0.99). The Old Confederacy infobox gives no area, so the old shapes cannot be checked.

Gaps (page silent or page budget of 14 spent): the Bernese Oberland, Aargau, Jura and Basel-Landschaft cells that enter in 1395, 1459, 1482, 1487, 1529 and the Tyrol/Vorarlberg fringe cells 1492-1526 are undated (confidence 1 or noted); the Valtellina's loss (July 1620) and recovery (3 September 1639) are now dated from the Graubunden page; Ossola and Blenio years; the Valais and Vaud cells that enter in 1482, 1529 and 1540 follow the cantonal areas, not a dated conquest; Neuchatel's two extra cells 1512-1528; the St. Gallen-area cells that enter 1459-1519 (no page); the diet seat 1815-1847 and the Mediation years (capitals; Frauenfeld from 1712/13 now on the Frauenfeld page); the 1860 Treaty of Turin neutral zone. Pages that would not load: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Lausanne_(1564) (url_not_found); the Duchy of Savoy page was opened as a replacement and was nearly silent. The Valais, St. Gallen, Aargau, Vaud and Italian Wars pages were not opened for lack of budget (14 pages spent). Names the gazetteer lacks: Grandson, Echallens (used as a radius), Toggenburg, Valtellina (used the province of Sondrio), Chablais, Pays de Gex, Upper Valais.

Repair pass 2026-10-25 (after the adversarial review of eu-09-f): (1) keyframe 1564-1571 now removes the Genevan-basin cells that /ledger loses to house-of-savoy in 1564. (2) Keyframes 1363-1475 are adjust: Solothurn (from 1363) and Fribourg (from 1459) are removed until their accession in 1481 (History of Switzerland and Old Swiss Confederacy), a new keyframe 1481 adds them. (3) The Mediation land 1803-1814 returns to this dossier from helvetic-republic on 19 February 1803 (four new keyframes); the 1815 gains are Neuchatel, the Jura (from France), Geneva, and the Valais (4 August 1815); helvetic-republic (eu-20) must end on 19 February 1803. (4) Neuchatel is drawn Swiss from 1815 (canton and Prussian principality at once until 1848); kingdom-of-prussia (eu-09) must mirror; the 1848 event is a rename. (5) Geneva's 1815-16 additions: six French communes (Treaty of Paris, 20 November 1815, bourbon-kingdom-of-france) and the Savoyard communes (Treaty of Turin, 1816, kingdom-of-sardinia), narrowed regions; the grid cannot separate them from the old republic. (6) The Upper Valais is the 1416 associate; the Lower Valais joins in November 1475 (county-of-savoy loses it to sieben-zenden). The Canton of Valais page dates the associate status to 12 March 1529, against 1416 on the Old Swiss Confederacy page: 1416 kept at confidence 2. (7) Counterparts: Bellinzona (1500) and the Ossola (1516) are now kingdom-of-france (France held Milan 1499-1512 and from 1515; eu-10 needs a loss in 1500 and a gain in 1516); Appenzell, Schaffhausen and Basel are holy-roman-empire-minor-states. (8) Valtellina tint broken 1620-1639; Diet seat Frauenfeld 1713-1798 (Zurich only presided). Left as they were: the Chablais, Ternier and Gaillard cells of 1536-1564 (Chablais, Pays de Gex and Emmanuel Philibert pages are silent); the 1395, 1497 (Blenio) and 1512 (Ossola) cells (Sempach, Blenio District and Ossola pages silent); keyframes 1482, 1487, 1492, 1519, 1526 and 1529 (Canton of St. Gallen page silent on Sargans, Rheintal and Werdenberg).
